# HR Industry Core Conclusions

| Dimension | Current knowledge |
| --- | --- |
| Industry role | HCM/HRMS manages the employee lifecycle from recruitment and onboarding through attendance, performance and payroll. |
| Best-fit demand | Organisations with high turnover, multiple sites, shift or field work and payroll rules that depend on attendance data. |
| Priority segments | Advanced manufacturing, chain retail/catering and logistics/warehousing are the first priority segments; hotels/tourism and IT/professional services are secondary. |
| Market stage | HCM is moving from cloud adoption toward AI-assisted workflows, suite integration, local payroll rules and auditable automation. |
| Data boundary | Industry value-added and employment indicators are customer-pool proxies, not HCM SaaS TAM. IDC and Gartner market estimates use separate scopes. |
| Compliance baseline | HR systems handle identity, salary, attendance, performance and potentially biometric data; purpose limitation, access control, retention and human review are essential. |
| Durable opportunity | Industry templates, attendance-to-payroll closure, local rule engines, implementation speed and cross-border compliance are more durable than AI features alone. |
